import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Pointwise.Set.Scalar
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Units.Defs
import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Defs
import Mathlib.Topology.Constructions
import Mathlib.Topology.Defs.Basic

set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference

/-!
# Direct-sum-of-fields presentations of tensor-packets (taxis #43, #45)

A local tensor-packet of log-shells (IUT III, Propositions 3.1–3.3) is, at each rational
place `v_Q` and each capsule `S` of the procession, the tensor product over `j ∈ S` of
direct sums over `v ∣ v_Q` of local fields. As a module with integral structure this
tensor product is **presented as a finite direct sum of fields**, each summand carrying
its holomorphic integral structure `O`; IUT III, Remark 3.9.5 phrases the holomorphic
hull entirely in terms of such a presentation.

This module fixes that presentation as an interface: a finite family of (topological)
fields, one for each *component* of the packet, together with an integral structure in
each summand. It also defines the region classes on the total space that the later
modules operate on:

* arbitrary regions (`Set` of the total space), with Borel-measurable regions singled
  out via `IsBorelRegion`;
* direct-product [pre-]regions (`IsProductRegion`), the class from which the log-volume
  combination laws of taxis #44 are stated;
* the scaled-integral regions `a·O` with every component of `a` nonzero
  (`IsHullRegion`), among which the holomorphic hull of taxis #45 is the least one.

## Honesty boundary

The identification of an actual tensor-packet `⊗_{j ∈ S} (⊕_{v ∣ v_Q} log(F_v))` with a
direct sum of fields (semisimple decomposition of tensor products of local fields) is
**not** proved here; it is part of the local-field infrastructure tracked in taxis #4
(`lana-agents/padic-log-volume`). This module only fixes the interface through which the
container consumes such a presentation; every instantiation obligation is an explicit
structure field of the container data (taxis #43).

## Source correspondence

* Presentation as a direct sum of fields with integral structure `O`: IUT III,
  Remark 3.9.5, first display and part (i).
* Direct-product [pre-]regions vs arbitrary (measurable) regions: IUT III,
  Proposition 3.9 and Remark 3.9.5(ii).
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Iut

universe u v

/-- A **direct-sum-of-fields presentation** with integral structures: for each component
`c` of a finite index type `C`, a topological field `Summand c` with a designated
integral structure `integral c` (the *holomorphic integral structure* `O` of the
summand).

In the intended instantiation `C` is the set of tuples `(v_j)_{j ∈ S}` of places
`v_j ∣ v_Q` indexed by the labels of a capsule `S`, and `Summand c` is the corresponding
tensor factor field of the semisimple decomposition of the tensor-packet
(IUT III, Remark 3.9.5). -/
structure DirectSumPresentation (C : Type u) : Type (max u (v + 1)) where
  /-- The summand field at component `c`. -/
  Summand : C → Type v
  /-- Each summand is a commutative ring: a field, or — for the tensor products of
  local fields that present the tensor-packets (IUT III, Proposition 3.1) — a finite
  product of fields. Nonzero components of hull regions are accordingly *units*. -/
  [ring_summand : ∀ c, CommRing (Summand c)]
  /-- Each summand carries a topology (used for the relative-compactness hypotheses of
  the holomorphic hull, taxis #45). -/
  [topology_summand : ∀ c, TopologicalSpace (Summand c)]
  /-- The holomorphic integral structure `O` of each summand: the ring of integers of a
  nonarchimedean summand (a subring), the unit ball of an archimedean one (a subset,
  IUT IV, Proposition 1.5(iii)). Carried as a set so that both cases are covered. -/
  integral : ∀ c, Set (Summand c)

attribute [instance] DirectSumPresentation.ring_summand
  DirectSumPresentation.topology_summand

namespace DirectSumPresentation

variable {C : Type u} (P : DirectSumPresentation.{u, v} C)

/-- The total space of a direct-sum-of-fields presentation. Since the component index is
finite in every intended instantiation, the direct sum is the plain dependent product. -/
def Total : Type (max u v) := ∀ c, P.Summand c

instance : TopologicalSpace P.Total := inferInstanceAs (TopologicalSpace (∀ c, P.Summand c))

/-- The holomorphic integral region `⊕_c O_c` of the presentation: the set of vectors
with every component in the integral structure of its summand. -/
def integralRegion : Set P.Total := {x | ∀ c, x c ∈ P.integral c}

/-- A **direct-product [pre-]region**: a region of the total space which is the product
of one region in each summand field (IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(ii) distinguishes these from
arbitrary regions). -/
def IsProductRegion (R : Set P.Total) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : ∀ c, Set (P.Summand c), R = {x | ∀ c, x c ∈ U c}

/-- The product region attached to a family of component regions. -/
def productRegion (U : ∀ c, Set (P.Summand c)) : Set P.Total := {x | ∀ c, x c ∈ U c}

/-- The scaled integral region `a · O`: the set of vectors whose `c`-component lies in
`a c • O_c` for every component `c`. For `a` with every component nonzero these are the
candidate holomorphic hulls of IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i). -/
def scaledIntegral (a : P.Total) : Set P.Total :=
  {x | ∀ c, x c ∈ a c • P.integral c}

/-- A **hull region**: a region of the form `a · O` with every component of `a` a
unit — nonzero in every field factor (IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)). The holomorphic hull
of a region `U` is the least hull region containing `U`; see `Iut.HullSystem`. -/
def IsHullRegion (R : Set P.Total) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : P.Total, (∀ c, IsUnit (a c)) ∧ R = P.scaledIntegral a

end DirectSumPresentation

end Iut

end AbcAdaptation.Reference
payload.natural_language_statement:
**Formal-code readback**

**English**

All declarations are in the namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut. Let u and v be universe levels and let C : Type u be an arbitrary index type. DirectSumPresentation C is a structure in Type (max u (v + 1)). It consists of a family Summand : C → Type v; for every c : C, a commutative ring structure with identity on Summand(c); for every c : C, a topological-space structure on Summand(c); and a family integral assigning an arbitrary subset integral(c) ⊆ Summand(c) to every c. The ring_summand and topology_summand fields are registered as typeclass instances, so these structures are available after a presentation is fixed. There is no finiteness or nonemptiness hypothesis on C. No axiom relates the topologies to the ring operations, and no algebraic or topological condition is imposed on the subsets integral(c). In particular, the rings are not required to be nontrivial.

Fix P : DirectSumPresentation C. The definition Total(P) : Type (max u v) is the dependent function type ∀ c : C, P.Summand(c): an element x supplies one coordinate x(c) in each summand. The explicitly provided topological-space instance is the product topology inherited from this dependent function type. Despite the structure's identifier, Total is a full dependent product; the definition imposes no finite-support condition and does not require C to be finite.

The definition integralRegion(P) is the subset of Total(P) consisting of those x such that, for every c : C, x(c) ∈ P.integral(c). For any R ⊆ Total(P), IsProductRegion(P,R) is the proposition that there exists a family of subsets U, with U(c) ⊆ P.Summand(c) for each c, for which R = {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)}. The existential quantifier chooses one family U for the whole set R; no uniqueness is required. Conversely, for every such family U, productRegion(P,U) is exactly {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)}. Neither definition requires the coordinate subsets to be open, closed, nonempty, or to have any other regularity.

For any a : Total(P), scaledIntegral(P,a) is the subset {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • P.integral(c)}. Here the set action is multiplication by a(c) in the ring P.Summand(c): membership at coordinate c means that there exists b ∈ P.integral(c) with a(c) · b = x(c). The definition scaledIntegral itself puts no unit or nonzero condition on a. For any R ⊆ Total(P), IsHullRegion(P,R) means that there exists one a : Total(P) such that every a(c) is a unit in its ring and R = scaledIntegral(P,a). Being a unit means having a multiplicative inverse; it is not a separate nonzero assumption, and in a trivial ring zero is a unit. The multiplier family a is not required to be unique. The equality is equality with that one scaled set; the definition states no minimality, closure operation, or condition of containing a separately given region, and no holomorphic condition occurs.

Empty and unrestricted cases follow directly from these definitions. If C is empty, Total(P) has exactly one element, all universal coordinate conditions are vacuous, and integralRegion, every productRegion, and every scaledIntegral are the whole Total(P). In that case IsProductRegion(P,R) and IsHullRegion(P,R) each hold exactly when R is the whole singleton Total(P). If C has a coordinate c₀ with P.integral(c₀) empty, integralRegion and every scaledIntegral are empty; the empty region then satisfies IsHullRegion by taking a(c) = 1 at every coordinate. For a nonempty C, an empty coordinate subset in U makes productRegion(P,U) empty, so the empty region satisfies IsProductRegion. None of these predicates use the supplied topologies; topology is part of the presentation and of the Total instance, not an additional condition in the region formulas.

**简体中文**

所有声明均位于命名空间 AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut 中。设 u、v 为宇宙层级，C : Type u 为任意指标类型。DirectSumPresentation C 是位于 Type (max u (v + 1)) 中的结构，包含以下数据：类型族 Summand : C → Type v；对每个 c : C，在 Summand(c) 上给出的含幺交换环结构；对每个 c : C，在 Summand(c) 上给出的拓扑空间结构；以及集合族 integral，为每个 c 指定任意子集 integral(c) ⊆ Summand(c)。字段 ring_summand 和 topology_summand 被登记为类型类实例，因此固定该结构后即可使用这些环结构和拓扑结构。不要求 C 有限或非空。没有任何公理要求拓扑与环运算相容，也没有对各子集 integral(c) 施加代数或拓扑条件。特别地，不要求这些环非平凡。

固定 P : DirectSumPresentation C。定义 Total(P) : Type (max u v) 为依赖函数类型 ∀ c : C, P.Summand(c)；其元素 x 在每个指标 c 处给出坐标 x(c) ∈ P.Summand(c)。代码显式提供的拓扑空间实例是该依赖函数类型所带的乘积拓扑。尽管结构标识符中含有 DirectSum，Total 的实际定义是完整的依赖直积，没有有限支撑条件，也不要求 C 有限。

定义 integralRegion(P) 为 Total(P) 中满足以下条件的元素构成的子集：对每个 c : C，都有 x(c) ∈ P.integral(c)。对任意 R ⊆ Total(P)，IsProductRegion(P,R) 是如下命题：存在一个子集族 U，其中每个 U(c) ⊆ P.Summand(c)，使得 R = {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)}。这里的存在量词为整个集合 R 选择同一个集合族 U，不要求唯一性。反过来，对每个这样的集合族 U，productRegion(P,U) 就是集合 {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)}。这两个定义均不要求坐标子集为开集、闭集、非空集或具有其他正则性。

对任意 a : Total(P)，scaledIntegral(P,a) 定义为子集 {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • P.integral(c)}。这里对集合的作用是环 P.Summand(c) 中乘以 a(c) 的运算：坐标 c 处的成员条件等价于存在 b ∈ P.integral(c)，使 a(c) · b = x(c)。scaledIntegral 本身不要求 a 的坐标为可逆元或非零。对任意 R ⊆ Total(P)，IsHullRegion(P,R) 表示存在同一个 a : Total(P)，使每个 a(c) 都是所在环的可逆元，且 R = scaledIntegral(P,a)。可逆元是具有乘法逆元的元素；这里没有额外的非零假设，在平凡环中零也是可逆元。不要求乘子族 a 唯一。该等式只要求 R 等于某个这样的缩放集合；定义没有断言最小性、闭包运算或包含另一个给定区域，也没有全纯条件。因此，标识符中的包络不应自行解释为全纯包络。

空集等边界情形由定义直接确定。若 C 为空，Total(P) 恰有一个元素，所有逐坐标的全称条件都自然成立，integralRegion、任意 productRegion 和任意 scaledIntegral 都等于整个 Total(P)。此时，IsProductRegion(P,R) 和 IsHullRegion(P,R) 均当且仅当 R 是整个单点集 Total(P) 时成立。若存在指标 c₀ 使 P.integral(c₀) 为空，则 integralRegion 和任意 scaledIntegral 均为空；此时逐坐标取 a(c) = 1，即可使空区域满足 IsHullRegion。若 C 非空且 U 的某个坐标子集为空，则 productRegion(P,U) 为空，因而空区域满足 IsProductRegion。这些谓词均不使用给定的拓扑；拓扑属于结构数据并用于 Total 的拓扑实例，而不是区域公式中的额外条件。

**日本語**

すべての宣言は名前空間 AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut に属する。u、v を宇宙レベルとし、C : Type u を任意の添字の型とする。DirectSumPresentation C は Type (max u (v + 1)) に属する構造であり、型の族 Summand : C → Type v、各 c : C に対する Summand(c) 上の単位元を持つ可換環構造、各 c : C に対する Summand(c) 上の位相空間構造、および各 c に任意の部分集合 integral(c) ⊆ Summand(c) を割り当てる族 integral からなる。フィールド ring_summand と topology_summand は型クラスのインスタンスとして登録されており、この構造を固定すると各環構造と位相構造が利用できる。C の有限性や非空性は仮定しない。位相と環演算の両立性を課す公理はなく、部分集合 integral(c) に代数的・位相的条件も課さない。特に、環が非自明であることは要求されない。

P : DirectSumPresentation C を固定する。Total(P) : Type (max u v) は依存関数の型 ∀ c : C, P.Summand(c) と定義される。その要素 x は、各添字 c において座標 x(c) ∈ P.Summand(c) を与える。明示的に与えられる位相空間のインスタンスは、この依存関数の型の積位相である。構造の識別子に DirectSum が含まれるが、Total の実際の定義は依存直積の全体であり、有限台の条件も C の有限性も要求しない。

integralRegion(P) は、すべての c : C について x(c) ∈ P.integral(c) を満たす x からなる Total(P) の部分集合である。任意の R ⊆ Total(P) に対し、IsProductRegion(P,R) は、各 U(c) が P.Summand(c) の部分集合であるような族 U が存在して、R = {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)} となるという命題である。存在量化は集合 R 全体に対して一つの族 U を選ぶものであり、一意性は要求しない。また、このような任意の族 U に対し、productRegion(P,U) は集合 {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ U(c)} そのものである。いずれの定義も、各座標の部分集合が開集合、閉集合、非空集合であることや、その他の正則性を要求しない。

任意の a : Total(P) に対し、scaledIntegral(P,a) は部分集合 {x | ∀ c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • P.integral(c)} である。集合への作用は環 P.Summand(c) における a(c) による乗法であり、座標 c における所属条件は、ある b ∈ P.integral(c) が存在して a(c) · b = x(c) となることである。scaledIntegral 自体は a の座標が可逆元であることも零でないことも要求しない。任意の R ⊆ Total(P) に対し、IsHullRegion(P,R) は、ある一つの a : Total(P) が存在して、各 a(c) がその環の可逆元であり、R = scaledIntegral(P,a) となることを意味する。可逆元とは乗法逆元を持つ元であり、別に零でないことを仮定しているわけではない。自明な環では零も可逆元である。乗数の族 a の一意性は要求されない。この等式はそのように座標ごとに乗算して得られる一つの集合との一致を述べるだけであり、最小性、閉包操作、別に指定された領域の包含は述べない。正則性に関する条件もなく、識別子の Hull を正則包と解釈する根拠はこのコードにはない。

空の場合などの境界事例も定義から決まる。C が空ならば Total(P) の要素はちょうど一つであり、すべての座標に関する全称条件は空虚に成り立つ。integralRegion、任意の productRegion、任意の scaledIntegral はすべて Total(P) 全体に等しい。このとき IsProductRegion(P,R) と IsHullRegion(P,R) は、いずれも R が一元集合 Total(P) 全体である場合に限って成り立つ。ある添字 c₀ で P.integral(c₀) が空ならば、integralRegion と任意の scaledIntegral は空である。この場合、各座標で a(c) = 1 とすれば、空の領域は IsHullRegion を満たす。C が非空で U のある座標の部分集合が空ならば、productRegion(P,U) は空であり、空の領域は IsProductRegion を満たす。これらの述語は、与えられた位相を使用しない。位相は構造のデータおよび Total の位相インスタンスを構成するが、領域の式に付加された条件ではない。

**Paper source context (English; separate from the formal-code readback)**

**Paper source context.** Mochizuki III, Proposition 3.1 (pp. 92–93), describes local tensor packets, their ring decompositions, and integral structures. Remark 3.9.5 (pp. 126–127) then defines holomorphic hulls in that arithmetic setting. Item (i) retains a finite-log-volume, relatively compact subset prerequisite. For a relatively compact input it chooses the smallest containing region obtained by scaling the integral structure by an element nonzero in every field component. For an input that is not relatively compact, the paper instead assigns the full ambient space. Both branches belong to the quoted paper definition.

**Implementation scope.** DirectSumPresentation is only an interface: an arbitrary index type $C$, component commutative rings $A_c$, a topology on each component, and designated subsets $O_c$. It does not require $C$ to be finite, the rings to be fields, the ring operations to be continuous, or the subsets to be actual integer rings. Its total space is the dependent product. Product regions impose separate component conditions. IsHullRegion means $R=aO$ for a componentwise invertible multiplier. In a field, invertible agrees with nonzero. In a nontrivial commutative ring a unit is nonzero, while a nonzero element need not be a unit; the carrier also allows trivial rings, where zero is a unit. This bundle neither constructs the paper’s tensor decomposition nor provides the qualification, leastness, or full-space branch of the paper’s hull operation.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III: Canonical Splittings of the Log-theta-lattice* (May 2020), Remark 3.9.5, complete opening paragraph; printed/PDF page(s) 126.

> In situations that involve consideration of various sorts of regions [cf. the discussion of Remarks 3.1.1, (iii), (iv); 3.9.4] to which the log-volume may be applied, it is often of use to consider the notion of the holomorphic hull of a region.

Transcription: visually checked; line breaks and typography are normalized as recorded in the source evidence.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III: Canonical Splittings of the Log-theta-lattice* (May 2020), Remark 3.9.5(i), complete item; printed/PDF page(s) 127.

> Suppose that we are in the situation of Proposition 3.9, (i). Let
>
> $$ {}^{\alpha}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})\quad\text{(respectively, }{}^{A}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}});\quad{}^{A,\alpha}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v})\text{)} $$
>
> be a subset that contains a relatively compact subset whose log-volume [cf. the discussion of Remark 3.1.1, (iii), (iv), as well as Remark 3.9.7, (ii), below] is finite [i.e., $>-\infty$]. If ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) is relatively compact, then we define the holomorphic hull of ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) to be the smallest subset of the form
>
> $$ {}^{\alpha}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}}}\quad\text{(respectively, }{}^{A}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}}};\quad{}^{A,\alpha}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v}}\text{)} $$
>
> — where, relative to the direct sum decomposition of $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}((-))$ as a direct sum of fields [cf. the discussion of Proposition 3.9, (i)], $\lambda\in\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}((-))$ is an element such that each component of $\lambda$ [i.e., relative to this direct sum decomposition] is nonzero — that contains ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$). If ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) is not relatively compact, then we define the holomorphic hull of ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) to be $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})$ (respectively, $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})$; $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v})$). One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined [under the conditions stated].

Transcription: visually checked; line breaks and typography are normalized as recorded in the source evidence.

**Actual consumer.** The presentation and region predicates feed the large volume container, LogVolumeData, and LocalEstimate. The resulting dependency paths reach theorem110. The paper’s use of a hull volume is explicit in IV, Theorem 1.10, proof Step (iv) (p. 26); the formal numerical theorem receives the corresponding local estimates as premises.

These Definitions are detached source preparation; the consumer paths describe the original reference graph and do not establish live mission-root membership or S2-04 completion.
